2. Write the title of the postmortem document using the suggested naming convention, which typically includes the service name (in this case, `payments`), the date and time of the outage, and a brief description (e.g., `payments-2023-03-01_00:00-Outage-Root-Cause-Analysis`).

3. Determine the directory in which the postmortem should reside based on where similar documents are stored in your organization. This could be a shared folder on a cloud storage service or an internal repository.

4. Compile the relevant information about the outage, including the context, timeline of events, root cause analysis, resolution, and recommendations for future prevention. This information can be collected from various sources such as monitoring tools, logs, chat history, and any other relevant communication during the outage.

5. Organize the compiled information using the chosen template to create a clear and concise postmortem document.

6. Assign the reviewers based on who was on call during the outage. These individuals should have been involved in addressing the issue and will be able to provide valuable feedback and suggestions for improvement.

7. Share the completed postmortem document with the assigned reviewers, ensuring that they have enough time to review it thoroughly and provide their feedback.

8. Incorporate the feedback received from the reviewers into the postmortem document, making any necessary revisions or updates.

9. Once the postmortem document has been finalized, distribute it to the appropriate stakeholders within your organization, such as team members, managers, and executive leadership.

10. Schedule a meeting to discuss the findings and recommendations from the postmortem document, addressing any questions or concerns that may arise and outlining the next steps for implementing the recommended changes to prevent similar outages in the future.
